Verifier notes and special checks

Fifty-six printed bars, all full bars of three quarter-note beats in 3/4. The first six systems have six bars each and the last four systems have five. The upper staff opens in treble and the lower staff in bass, with two sharps. A light-light double bar closes the eighth bar. The twenty-fourth bar ends with a cautionary treble clef on the lower staff and a light-light double bar; one flat is printed after that bar and reprinted, with the treble clef, at the start of the next system. The lower staff returns to bass immediately before the barline of the fortieth bar. A light-light double bar closes the forty-eighth bar, and the next bar begins with two sharps. The fifty-sixth bar ends with a thin-and-thick final barline. Every system closes with a barline through both staves. The crops keep the tempo, dynamics, slurs, and stems, and leave the title, page number, and publisher line outside the musical systems.

  • System 2, right barline of P008: Do the two vertical strokes add an extra bar? No. Both strokes pass through both staves and form one light-light double bar. No repeat dots are printed beside them.
  • System 4, after the double bar of P024: Is the ink in the right margin another barline? No. After the double bar both staves print one flat. That signature is reprinted at the start of system 5. It is not a bar.
  • System 6, barline between P032 and P033: Does the stroke at crop x 640 pass through both staves? Yes. It crosses the upper staff and the lower staff at the same x. The dynamic sits between the staves and does not break the stroke into a stem.
  • System 9, right barline of P048: Do the two strokes before the sharps add an extra bar? No. They are one light-light double bar. P049 begins on the same system with two sharps on both staves.
  • System 10, end of P056: Is the thick stroke a separate bar from the thin stroke? No. The thin stroke and the thick stroke together are the final barline. The bar holds a dotted half-note chord under fermatas, which fills three quarter-note beats.
  • All ten systems: Does any system end without a barline through both staves? No. Each system begins and ends with a barline through both staves, so no bar is split by a system break. No repeat, ending, pickup, or meter change is printed after the opening 3/4.
